title: One Chinese Teapot Sold for $2 Million — No Glaze at All | China Travel Expert
description:
One Chinese clay teapot sold for about $2 million — and it has no glaze at all.

This is a Yixing zisha (宜兴紫砂) purple-clay teapot. Under a microscope the unglazed clay shows a rare "double-pore" structure — open and closed pores together — that lets the pot breathe. That breathability keeps tea from stewing the way it can in sealed glass or glazed ceramic, smoothing out bitterness and giving the tea a silkier body. The best clay comes from Huanglong Mountain in Yixing, Jiangsu, and a 1948 purple-clay pot by master Gu Jingzhou fetched roughly $2 million at auction in 2010.

🧭 Expert Tip: If you want a real one, buy zisha in Yixing itself (Jiangsu) or from a trusted specialist — most cheap "purple clay" pots are dyed or coated, not true zisha.
